title: Saving Early for College with Compound Interest
learningObjectives: Describe how time and compound interest can increase savings for post-secondary education.
Use a calculator to show how principal, interest rate, compounding frequency, and time affect savings growth.

evidence.quote: Compound interest is when you earn interest on both the money you save and the interest you earn.

explanations.text: Compound interest means you earn interest on both the money you save and the interest you earn, so starting early helps education savings grow.

evidence.quote: After the first year, you would have $1,050—your original principal, plus 5 percent, or $50.
The second year, you would have $1,102.50.

explanations.text: For example, $1,000 at 5 percent compounded once a year becomes $1,050 after one year and $1,102.50 in the second year.

evidence.quote: Increasing the compounding frequency or your interest rate or adding to your principal can help your savings grow even faster.
The sooner you start saving for post-secondary education, the faster your money can grow from compound interest.

explanations.text: Raising the compounding frequency, interest rate, or principal can help savings grow even faster, so starting early for post-secondary education helps.

predictions.prompt: If you save $1,000 at 5% compounded yearly for 10 years, how much will you have?
If you save $2,000 at 4% compounded quarterly for 8 years, how much will you have?
